I was at a conference in Los Angeles a few years ago where Walter
Baumgartner demonstrated the water thread experiment....using high velocity

around the nozzle that consisted of orbiting very fine water droplets....it
all glowed with a pale blue light in the dark of the room.
He said the amount of levitation and intensity of glow was directly
proportionate to the 'zeta potential' of the water....that is how much
energy the water could hold....he said the water in LA was really poor
quality because the water thread experiment usually produced spectacular
results. I have a bad photo of the levitating ring from an old Borderlands
magazine.
A similar effect occurs with water knives where they squirt water out at
something on the order of 40-50,000 psi.....extremely high voltages are
produced which requires the head and nozzle to be grounded for safety.
There are also old documents describing using high speed water and steam as
electrical generators using this ripping apart of the molecules that
releases the electricity (Lenard discovered this).

report in the journal Science.

Found this from Gerald O'Docharty in the message base, never realized
there was such a drastic difference. The curie point is a temperature
where magnets lose their magnetic field entirely, though when they cool
down, the magnetism is restored. My understanding is for normal ferrite
magnets, the curie point is about 180 degreed F. So I was surprised to
see this comment;
The fact of the matter is however that the curie point for most ND
magnets IS 300 degrees C. I have several data books from Big time magnet
manufacturers that specify this explicitly, as well as having followed
the trade journals for years. This is the main disadvantage as a matter
of fact with the Neodymium -Iron -Boron magnets when used in
applications such as motors where there is the chance of a high
temperature rise. Although they have the strongest MGOe rating of any
industrial magnetic material and are used in some servo motors, special
care has to be taken to insure they dont get too hot, or they will
suffer irreversible demagnetisation. this is why most motors that
specify rare earth magnets are using Samarium Cobalt. Its curie
temperature is typically 680-700 degrees C.
----------------

increase, but I don't know if it stays that way once brought back to
room temperature. Just thinking along the lines of other ways to bring

sheet metal laying on the botton to serve as the cathode. Nickel or
platinum beads are placed on top of the nickel plate which fill the

non-conducting plastic. Over this plastic is placed the honeycomb

carbonate electrolyte is poured into the container halfway up the
catalytic converter.

power supply, the cell will at first draw much amps until it heats up
and then the power to run it will be less than the energy output (in the

taken it from the top, for now, a month later, a very odd thing has

The 'mysterious spinner' is not mysterious at all...Lee posted this to
the KeelyNet BBS many years ago...at the time, we were all amazed but
experiments showed the truth of it.
Basically, take a thread, connect it to the paper clip and hold it near
one end of a magnet...as you bring the clip closer to the pole, it will
begin to spin.....until it winds up on the thread, then it will stop
spinning as torsional forces balance.
When you do this with a monofilament, there is NO SPIN....Charles Yost
said it was most likely the twist of the fibers making up the
thread....when under pressure, caused by the attraction of the clip to
the magnet, the clip spins....
Lee made a very neat clear tube with a spring loaded plunger on one
end...attached to the plunger is a paper clip connected by a thread...on
the other end of the clear tube is a magnet....when you push the plunger
down, the clip is brought close to the magnet and it will wind up and
eventually stop....let the plunger go and the clip will unspin to an at
rest state...what makes it neat is the clip floating in the air from the
pull of the magnet....
I am surprised they are selling these...but they are neat toys...

I was just looking at an old picture of a Dirod type electrostatic
generator I made about 20 years ago. It made me remember about a
peculiar behaviour of the machine. It was constructed so that it was
driven by a belt from a motor, but it could be turned by hand with the
belt off and still work. Well it could be spun this way by hand and sort
of 'wound up' to a point where the voltage was at maximum before
breakdown. If the axle was let go at that point, it would spin on its
own in the reverse direction untill the static charge was used up, often
20 or 30 revolutions or so. I could have theoretically connected a high
voltage DC supply to it and it would have run indefinitely. Has anyone
seen a practical application of this? Do the plastic disc e-s machines
behave the same way?
I don't have that machine anymore, the fellow I loaned it to died and I
didn't want to ask for it back. It would be simple to build another
though.
-Gerald O'

Although I don't think that all the mechanisms are known there are a
number of hints that waves are involved in various events of this type.
* A study in Budapest and reported in "Cycles" found strong correlations
between the presence of 3 Hz waves and the number of accidents as
measured by ambulance call outs. Another study found that the presence
of ~3 Hz waves slows human reaction times while ~12 Hz speeds them up.
It seems evident that these waves can entrain the brain and cause its
clock to run at the wrong speed for controlling the body.
* As discovered by Piccardi, Tanaka, Shnol' and others; certain
chemical, biological and atomic phenomena are variable to cosmic
influences and often show cyclical relationships or effects due to the
sun or cosmic rays.
* We might add to that Chizhevsky's work on war having cycles of 11, 22
years etc.
In these areas of study it is generally found that there are high
correlations around the world and so this certainly lends itself to
study by statistical means. To the extent that a cyclical basis can be
established we might be able to avoiding getting on planes or boats or
doing hazardous thinks. I for one don't intend to be around when the
next extinction cycle strikes in 13 million years :-)
